  # ─── Section A — Pipeline / Stage Composition (8 keepers) ──────────────
  - id: a-1
    title: "[A] Wrap stage handlers as kind: agent plugins"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper, agent-plugin]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §A"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/sw-pipeline.sh:1572 (run_stage_with_retry dispatch); legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-stages-{intake,build,review,delivery,monitor}.sh"

  - id: a-2

    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper, orchestrator-plugin]

    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-intelligence.sh:2042-2195"

      untested-functions check) as a non-cyclic, fail-fast plugin that runs
      before the audit-plan selection. Must abort the compound_quality cycle
      if any gate fails.
    plugin_kind: "orchestrator"
  - id: a-3
    title: "[A] Split compound_quality into audit-plan selection plugin"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper, orchestrator-plugin]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §A"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-intelligence.sh:2028-2036 (entry); :429-508 (pipeline_select_audits)"
    behavior: |
      Audit-plan selection: reads quality-scores.jsonl history and branches
      audit intensity (lightweight/targeted/full) on avg score. Preserves the
      real history query at :453-482 and intensity adjustment at :470-480.
    plugin_kind: "orchestrator"
  - id: a-4
    title: "[A] Split compound_quality into cycle/plateau loop plugin"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper, orchestrator-plugin]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §A"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-intelligence.sh:2198+"
    behavior: |
      The main compound-quality cycle: run audits, accumulate findings, detect
      plateau (same finding count twice → stop), detect divergence (count
      increases → reduce), respect adaptive cycle limits.
    plugin_kind: "orchestrator"
  - id: a-5
    title: "[A] Extract compound_quality backtrack-to-stage as its own concern"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §A"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-intelligence.sh — backtrack embedded in cycle loop"
    behavior: |
      The backtrack-to-stage logic (architecture findings → route to design,
      scope violations → override everything) is currently embedded in the
      cycle loop. Lift it out so cycle/plateau and backtrack don't share
      state. (Superseded: the backward edge is `route_back`, ADR-045;
      `kind: recovery` was retired by #1900.)
  - id: a-6
    title: "[A] Preserve gate semantics (auto / approve / budget / score / scope / smoke)"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §A"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-stages.sh (gate declarations in templates)"
    behavior: |
      Six gate kinds, declared in templates not in handlers. Thresholds in JSON.
      Quality score = 100 - 20·crit - 10·major - 2·minor, hard floor 40, strict
      mode 70 + zero-critical. Scope gate enforced at 3 layers (prompt-injected
      constraint, safe_git_stage block, review fail-closed count).
  - id: a-7
    title: "[A] Preserve template subtractive composition (hotfix disables stages)"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §A, ADR-009"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/config/pipeline-templates/ + legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-stages.sh"
    behavior: |
      Hotfix template is subtractive (disables plan/design/review, keeps CQ).
      Same handler code, different composition. Preserve the pattern.

      ADR-009 update: templates use `extends: <base>` + `disabled_stages: [...]`
      + `stage_overrides: {...}` rather than copying the base. Hotfix becomes:
        extends: standard
        disabled_stages: [plan, design, review]
        stage_overrides:
          build: { max_iterations: 10 }
  - id: a-8
    title: "[A] pipeline_should_skip_stage (5-signal switch) + bounded back-edge cap"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §A"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-intelligence.sh:32-126 (skip), :351-1604 (backtrack)"
    behavior: |
      pipeline_should_skip_stage reads 5 signals (complexity, labels, diff size,
      mid-pipeline reassessment, hard floor) and decides which stages to skip.
      pipeline_backtrack_to_stage allows bounded back-edges (cap=1 per run).
      Reassessment can simplify the pipeline mid-run.

    labels: [phase-1, keeper, learning-loop]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §B1.2"

  - id: b-3
    title: "[B1] Skill registry success-rate self-improvement (closed loop)"
    milestone: "Phase 4 — CLI, UX, Skills, Personas"
    labels: [phase-4, keeper, learning-loop]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §B1.3, §F"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/skill-memory.sh:144-176 (record + sort); legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/sw-pipeline.sh:1703 (recommendations consumed); legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-state.sh:325/608"

  - id: b-4
    title: "[B1] Two-phase complexity (initial LLM + post-build reassessment)"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper, learning-loop]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §B1.4"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/sw-intelligence.sh:533; legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-intelligence.sh:1238"

    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §B1.5"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/loop-convergence.sh:101-132 (check_circuit_breaker); legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/sw-pipeline-vitals.sh:56-59 (weights)"
    behavior: |
      check_circuit_breaker reads pipeline_compute_vitals() JSON at :108, branches
      on verdict=='abort' at :111. Real control, not just telemetry. Weights are
      env-tunable but static defaults — treat as configuration, not learned params.
  - id: b-6
    title: "[B1] Scope manifest as fenced markdown in design.md (artifact-as-contract)"
    milestone: "Phase 2 — Reliability & Safety Primitives"
    labels: [phase-2, keeper, safety-primitive]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §B1.6"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-stages.sh:42 (_extract_scope_from_design)"
    behavior: |
      Scope manifest is a fenced markdown block in design.md. Humans edit visually;
      engine parses with awk. Already partially wired in Phase 0 (chokepoint
      reads from a manifest path); this keeper verifies the design.md
      integration end-to-end.
  - id: b-7
    title: "[B1] Three-tier memory recall (goal → issue → repo) with ruflo HNSW backing"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper, learning-loop]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §B1.7"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-stages-build.sh:209; legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/ruflo-adapter.sh:2376-2440 (HNSW)"
    behavior: |
      Goal-scoped → issue-scoped → repo-scoped cascade. Native memory is TF-IDF
      (sw-memory.sh); ruflo-adapter provides HNSW vectors via MCP under
      per-repo / per-issue namespaces (legacy uses shipwright-* names; zBuild
      keeper will use zbuild-* namespaces to avoid cross-talk). Carry forward
      as side service.
    body_suffix: |
      ## ADR-011 / §6.5 cross-reference

      This cascade is now backend-agnostic: it queries `memory_search` per the
      [ADR-011](../../docs/adr/ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md) contract and
      inspects `memory_capabilities` to decide between text and vector
      matching. SQLite default (#216) does TF-IDF; ruflo optional (#217) does
      HNSW. Namespace naming changes from legacy `shipwright-*` to
      `zbuild-{repo,issue,goal}`.
  - id: b-8
    title: "[B1] Adaptive cycle limits (convergence/divergence/plateau detection)"
    milestone: "Phase 1 — Pipeline & Intelligence"
    labels: [phase-1, keeper, learning-loop]
    spec_cite: "KEEPERS §B1.8"
    legacy_cite: "legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-intelligence.sh:351/1604"
    behavior: |
      Convergence rate >50% extends, divergence reduces, plateau (same count
      twice) stops, budget exhaustion caps to zero. Plateau predicate is already

    body: |
      Implement the orchestration loop that reads a pipeline template
      (config/templates/<name>.yaml), reads detected platforms from
      state/platforms.json, resolves each stage's roles → plugins via the
      ADR-009 resolver, and calls plugin hooks (init → run → finalize).

      Scope:
      - core/pipeline/runner.sh with run_pipeline(template, goal) entry point
      - Reads stage list from template YAML (role-based per ADR-009)
      - Reads state/platforms.json for detected platforms
      - Per stage: resolves roles via plat-3, dispatches per stage strategy
        (fanout / composite / sequential — see plat-9/10/11)
      - Handles failure: reads `disposition` (ADR-054 §6), decides retry/abort
      - Writes state via core/state/atomic.sh on every stage transition
      - Emits pipeline.{start,end,abort} + stage.{start,complete,fail} events

        stages:

          - id: output

  - id: mvp-5a

    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation, tool-plugin, cli-ux]
    body: |
      Make the MVP output stage (#87 / mvp-5) print findings to stdout when no
      explicit destination flag/env is provided. This is the smallest possible
      change that lets `zbuild pipeline start --goal "..." --scope ...` run
      end-to-end without GitHub auth or a `--issue` flag, which is the
      canonical first-run demo.

      Rationale:
      - Unix convention: tools print to stdout by default.
      - ADR-010 (CI/CLI parity): output destinations are abstracted; stdout
        is the lowest-common-denominator destination that needs no setup.
      - Testability: CI smoke can pipe `zbuild ... | tee audit.md` without
        a tracking issue / write token.
      - Removes the "what issue number do I pass?" friction for first-time
        users trying the MVP.

      Scope:
      - In plugins/tool/output-github-comment/plugin.sh: if neither
        $ZBUILD_ISSUE nor $ZBUILD_OUTPUT is set, print the rendered markdown
        report to stdout AND skip the gh comment / local file write.
      - Document the precedence in the plugin's README and in the MVP
        smoke-test docs: --issue > --output file > stdout default.
      - Test: tests/plugin-output-stdout-test.sh verifies that with both
        env vars unset, stdout contains the report and no gh CLI call
        is attempted (mocked gh fails the test if called).

      Out of scope:
      - The full destinations dispatch table (stdout/file/pr-comment/
        check-run/step-summary with per-destination on/off switches) —
        that's #213.
      - Renaming the plugin away from `output-github-comment/` — keep the
        directory name for now; #213 will rename to `output/` when it
        generalizes the dispatch.

      Dependencies:
      - Blocks: nothing critical; this is a polish issue that makes #87's
        MVP demo work without ceremony.
      - Depends on: #87 (mvp-5) landing first; this layers on top.

      Spec citation: ADR-010 §3 (output destination abstraction);
      this is the minimum slice of #213 needed for the MVP first run.

      Implemented: PR #239 (2026-05-25). Three-way dispatch added to
      plugins/tool/output-github-comment/plugin.sh — ZBUILD_ISSUE >

  - id: mvp-5b
    title: "[Phase 0.5] Fix security-lens hook signature mismatch (stage, state_file contract)"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation, agent-plugin]
    body: |
      security_lens_run was coded as a unit-testable inner function with
      signature (input, scope_manifest, output, artifact_dir). The pipeline
      runner dispatches all hooks as (stage, state_file), so $3 was unbound
      and the security-lens stage failed with rc=1 on every pipeline run.

      Fix:
      - Renamed the inner implementation to _security_lens_run_inner to keep
        it directly unit-testable with explicit paths.
      - Added a thin security_lens_run(stage, state_file) wrapper that derives
        artifact paths from state_dir = $(dirname "$state_file"), matching the
        established pattern in intake_run and output_run.
      - Artifact filename partitioned by ZBUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM so fanout runs
        write security-<platform>-findings.json and don't overwrite each other;
        both forms match the *-findings.json glob in the output plugin.
      - Tests updated: unit tests call _security_lens_run_inner directly;
        three new hook-contract tests exercise security_lens_run end-to-end
        including the platform-scoped filename case.

      Implemented: PR #240 (2026-05-24). 37 security-lens assertions passing.
      Pipeline smoke confirmed end-to-end: intake → security-lens → output all
      complete with findings.json produced and report rendered.
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Merged PR #240 (2026-05-24).'

  # ─── Phase 0.5 — Platform-aware modularity (ADR-009, 14 issues) ───────
  - id: plat-1
    title: "[Phase 0.5] ADR-009 manifest fields: platform + provides.role + platform_overrides + detect.signals"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation]
    state: closed
    closed_reason: |
      Shipped in PR #226 (issue #191). Manifest schema extended with optional
      platform, provides.role, platform_overrides, and detect.signals fields.
      yaml_get_list added to registry.sh. Backward-compatible with existing manifests.
    body: |
      Extend ADR-001 plugin manifest with four new OPTIONAL fields per ADR-009:
        - platform: ios|node|null      # null/omit = generic fallback
        - provides.role: <semantic>    # e.g., coder, tester, security-auditor
        - platform_overrides:          # per-platform config tweaks
            <platform>: { <key>: <override> }
        - detect:                      # declarative platform signals
            signals:
              files: [{pattern, strength}]
              directories: [{pattern, strength}]

      All four are optional. Plugins without `platform` default to null
      (generic, always-applicable). Plugins without `provides.role` are
      addressed by id only. Plugins without `detect.signals` aren't part of
      platform detection. Backward-compatible with all existing manifests.

      Scope:
      - Update core/plugin-registry/registry.sh: validate_manifest accepts new fields
      - Update yaml_get to read nested detect.signals arrays
      - Update plugins/agent/security-lens/manifest.yaml: declare role=security-auditor
      - Test: existing security-lens still passes; new fields validate correctly
  - id: plat-2
    title: "[Phase 0.5] Template schema YAML (role-based stages + strategy + extends)"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation]
    state: closed
    closed_reason: |
      Shipped in PR #226 (issue #192). config/templates/standard.yaml created
      with 3-stage fanout template. core/pipeline/template.sh implements load_template,
      template_stage_roles (inline + block YAML), and template_stage_strategy.
    body: |
      ADR-009 template schema. Templates are YAML at config/templates/<name>.yaml.

      Schema:
        id: <name>
        name: <human-readable>
        extends: <base-template> | null    # subtractive composition
        defaults:
          strategy: fanout                  # default multi-platform behavior
        disabled_stages: [...]              # for extends
        stage_overrides: {stage: {key: val}} # for extends
        stages:
          - id: <stage-id>
            gate: auto | approve | budget | score | scope | smoke
            roles: [<role-1>, <role-2>]
            strategy: fanout | composite | sequential   # override default
            config: {...}

      Stages reference ROLES not plugin ids. Runner resolves at dispatch time
      via plat-3 resolver. One template can serve many platforms.

      Scope:
      - Define schema in config/templates/_schema.yaml
      - Write config/templates/standard.yaml + hotfix.yaml (extends standard)
      - Tests verify schema parse + extends resolution + disabled_stages skip
      - Reference: ADR-009 §2
  - id: plat-3
    title: "[Phase 0.5] Resolver: resolve_plugin_for_role(role, platform) with fallback"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation]
    state: closed
    closed_reason: |
      Shipped in PR #226 (issue #193). core/pipeline/resolver.sh implements
      resolve_plugin_for_role with 2-pass resolution (platform-specific → generic
      fallback), semver tie-break, alphabetical id tie-break, and
      registry.role-unresolved event on miss.
    body: |
      Core function consumed by the pipeline runner (mvp-1). Given a role and
      a detected platform, returns the matching plugin directory.

      Algorithm (ADR-009 §3):
        1. Search plugins where provides.role == role AND platform == <p>
        2. Else search plugins where provides.role == role AND platform == null
        3. Else emit registry.role-unresolved event; caller decides

      Tie-breaking (multiple plugins claim same role+platform):
        - Highest version wins
        - Tie → alphabetical by id, with warning emitted

      Scope:
      - core/plugin-registry/registry.sh: resolve_plugin_for_role()
      - resolve_plugins_for_stage(stage, platforms) for multi-platform stages
      - Tests with fixture plugins covering: exact match, fallback, tie-break,
        not-found, multi-platform fan-out
  - id: plat-4
    title: "[Phase 0.5] core/detect/platforms.sh subsystem (detection engine, not plugin)"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation, safety-primitive]
    state: closed
    closed_reason: |
      Shipped in PR #226 (issue #194). core/detect/platforms.sh implements
      detect_platforms with hardcoded indicator patterns (ios/node/python/go),
      git-SHA cache, .zbuild/platforms.json overrides (applied on cache hit too),
      and generic floor. manifest detect.signals parsing deferred to Phase 1.
    body: |
      Engine subsystem (NOT a plugin stage). Runs before any stage dispatch.
      Reads platform plugins' detect.signals manifests + .zbuild/platforms.json
      config; walks repo; writes state/platforms.json.

      Scope:
      - core/detect/platforms.sh exporting detect_platforms(repo_root)
      - Reads .zbuild/platforms.json overrides + disable_detection list
      - Globs plugins/*/*/manifest.yaml; extracts detect.signals from each
      - Folder-level scan (NOT whole-repo); each top-level candidate folder
        gets a platform assignment
      - Conflict resolution via signal strength (high > medium > low)
      - Output: state/platforms.json = [{path, platform, source}, ...]
      - Emits detection.complete event with summary; detection.conflict on ties

      Source labels: "config" (override), "detected" (signal match),
      "fallback" (config.fallback_platform), "unknown" (warn + skip).

      Tests: monorepo fixture (ios/ + api/), pure-platform fixture, ambiguous
      fixture (Package.swift + package.json same folder), docs-only fixture.
  - id: plat-5
    title: "[Phase 0.5] Platform plugin pattern: declarative detection signals"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation]
    body: |
      Document + provide first example. A "platform plugin" is a kind:tool
      plugin (or kind:agent) whose manifest declares detect.signals. New
      platforms = drop a manifest, no core changes.

      Scope:
      - docs/platform-pack-pattern.md: how to declare a new platform
      - First example: plugins/tool/generic-platform-marker/ (the null-platform
        sentinel; ensures generic-only repos still produce a clean platform map)
      - Optional: plugins/tool/node-platform/ as a real example with signals
        files: [{pattern: package.json, strength: high}, {pattern: package-lock.json, strength: medium}]
        directories: [{pattern: node_modules/, strength: low}]
      - Tests verify detection picks up these manifests automatically
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Closed via GitHub (live state: closed at 2026-05-27T00:50:41Z). Recorded by manifest-sync.'
  - id: plat-6
    title: "[Phase 0.5] .zbuild/platforms.json config schema (overrides + disable + aliases)"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation]
    body: |
      Per-repo config file consumed by plat-4 detection.

      Schema:
        {
          "version": "1.0",
          "overrides": [
            {"path": "ios/", "platform": "ios", "reason": "..."}
          ],
          "disable_detection": ["app/vendor/"],
          "aliases": {"nodejs": "node"},
          "fallback_platform": null,
          "cost_overrides": {
            "ios": {"max_tokens_per_stage": 200000},
            "node": {"max_tokens_per_stage": 100000}
          }
        }

      Scope:
      - JSON schema validation in core/detect/platforms.sh
      - docs/platforms-config-schema.md with examples
      - .gitignore: state/platforms.detected.json (machine-generated)
      - Tests cover override-wins-over-detect, disable_detection, aliases
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Closed via GitHub (live state: closed at 2026-05-27T00:50:41Z). Recorded by manifest-sync.'
  - id: plat-13
    title: "[Phase 0.5] Detection conflict resolution + signal strength ranking"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation, safety-primitive]
    body: |
      When a folder matches signals for multiple platforms, rank by strength
      and pick the winner. Ties → emit detection.conflict event + use config
      override if present, else warn + use config.fallback_platform.

      Rules (ADR-009 §3):
        - Each signal has strength: high | medium | low
        - Sum signal strengths per candidate platform
        - Highest sum wins
        - Tie → emit detection.conflict event, then:
          - If .zbuild/platforms.json has override for this path → use it
          - Else if fallback_platform set → use it (warning)
          - Else → warn + mark folder "ambiguous", exclude from pipeline scope

      Scope:
      - Implementation in core/detect/platforms.sh
      - Event: detection.conflict {path, candidates, strengths, resolution}
      - CLI: zbuild detect platforms --explain shows resolution reasoning
      - Tests cover all conflict patterns
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Closed via GitHub (live state: closed at 2026-05-27T00:50:42Z). Recorded by manifest-sync.'
  # ─── Phase 1 — Orchestration strategies (3 issues) ─────────────────────
  - id: plat-9

  # ─── Phase 0.5 — CI/CLI parity (ADR-010, 6 issues) ────────────────────
  - id: cipar-1
    title: "[Phase 0.5] zbuild bootstrap command (rehydrate state, verify auth, validate lockfile, detect resume)"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation, cli-ux]
    body: |
      First half of the CI/CLI lifecycle (ADR-010). Run at the start of every
      CI job and (no-op'ish) locally. Restores state from cache, verifies
      prereqs and auth, validates plugin lockfile, AND detects whether a
      prior pipeline left interrupted resume state.

      Two-memory-model awareness (ARCHITECTURE §6.5):
      - PIPELINE-RESUME MEMORY: restores ~/.zbuild/state/{pipeline-state.json,
        events.jsonl, artifacts/*} via cache backend (cipar-3). After restore,
        checks pipeline-state.json's status field:
          - status: in_progress AND last_event recent → AUTO-RESUME mode;
            subsequent `zbuild pipeline start` continues from last good stage
          - status: complete OR cache miss → FRESH-START mode; pipeline starts
            from intake
          - status: failed AND retry policy allows → AUTO-RESUME with retry
            classification (uses adapt-8 failure classifier)
        Emits pipeline.resume.detected | pipeline.fresh-start event.
      - LEARNING MEMORY: ADR-011 backend init. Calls memory_capabilities() on
        configured backend; degrades to sqlite default if optional backend
        unreachable. Does NOT block pipeline run on learning memory issues.

      Scope:
      - scripts/zbuild: bootstrap subcommand
      - core/bootstrap/bootstrap.sh: orchestrates the above
      - In CI: detects $GITHUB_ACTIONS, calls cache backend (cipar-3)
      - Locally: cache-pull is local-noop but resume detection still runs
      - Doctor-style report at end (green/yellow/red per check + resume status)
      - Reusable Actions composite: .github/actions/bootstrap/action.yml
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Closed via PR #286 on 2026-05-26 — duplicate of #223 (closed when bootstrap shipped via PR #245).'
  - id: cipar-2
    title: "[Phase 0.5] zbuild teardown command (snapshot state, mark status, upload artifacts, summarize)"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation, cli-ux]
    body: |
      Second half of the CI/CLI lifecycle (ADR-010). Run at end of every CI
      job (always-runs via `if: always()`); minimal locally.

      Two-memory-model awareness (ARCHITECTURE §6.5):
      - PIPELINE-RESUME MEMORY: marks pipeline-state.json.status appropriately
        before snapshot:
          - If pipeline.end emitted with status=success → status: complete,
            cache slot eligible for reset on next run
          - If pipeline aborted / runner OOMd / signal killed → status:
            interrupted; next bootstrap auto-resumes from last good stage
          - If explicit abort (operator) → status: aborted; next bootstrap
            requires --force-resume to continue
        Snapshots state directory to cache backend.
      - LEARNING MEMORY: pushes learned patterns/embeddings to backend (only
        if backend supports persistence; sqlite always does, ruflo persists
        in its own store). Independent failure mode — learning push failure
        does NOT fail the job.

      Scope:
      - scripts/zbuild: teardown subcommand
      - core/bootstrap/teardown.sh: status-mark + snapshot + uploads + summary
      - In CI: writes to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY; uploads state/artifacts/* via
        actions/upload-artifact; updates PR comment marker (uses #56 contract)
      - Reusable Actions composite: .github/actions/teardown/action.yml
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Closed via PR #286 on 2026-05-26 — duplicate of #224 (closed when teardown shipped via PR #245).'

  # ─── Phase 0.5 — Explicit resume CLI surface (1 issue) ─────────────────
  - id: resume-1
    title: "[Phase 0.5] zbuild pipeline resume CLI + auto-resume policy"
    milestone: "Phase 0.5 — MVP Pipeline & Distribution"
    labels: [phase-0, foundation, cli-ux]
    body: |
      Explicit operator surface for resuming an interrupted pipeline. Most of
      the resume mechanics are in #36 (CURRENT_ITERATION persistence), adapt-10
      (checkpoint-based recovery), and cipar-1 (bootstrap auto-detection).
      This issue ties them together with a clean CLI verb + auto-resume policy.

      Two memory models (ARCHITECTURE §6.5) — this issue is PURELY about
      pipeline-resume memory (ADR-006). Learning memory (ADR-011) is unaffected.

      Scope:
      - `zbuild pipeline resume [--run-id <id>] [--from-stage <stage>] [--force]`
        - With no args: resume the most recent in_progress/interrupted run
        - With --run-id: resume specific run
        - With --from-stage: skip ahead (operator override; emits warning event)
        - --force: ignore status=aborted; resume anyway
      - Auto-resume policy in cipar-1 bootstrap:
        - pipeline-state.json.status == in_progress AND last event < 24h ago
          → bootstrap returns "resume mode"; subsequent `pipeline start`
          auto-resumes unless --no-resume passed
        - status == interrupted (clean teardown saw OOM/signal) → auto-resume
        - status == aborted (operator-cancelled) → fresh-start unless --resume
        - status == complete → always fresh-start
      - In CI: cipar-1 bootstrap detects resume state in cache; runs pipeline
        with --resume implicit; teardown updates status appropriately
      - `zbuild pipeline status [--run-id <id>]` shows what would resume + why
      - Tests: kill -9 mid-stage scenario; verify resume continues at the
        failed stage (not at intake)

      Dependencies: cipar-1 (bootstrap), cipar-2 (teardown), #36
      (CURRENT_ITERATION), adapt-10 (checkpoint-based recovery).
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Closed via GitHub (live state: closed at 2026-05-25T12:00:17Z). Recorded by manifest-sync.'

    labels: [phase-0, foundation, cli-ux]
    body: |
      Self-healing manifest. Catches drift caused by humans (web UI closes,
      hand-merged PRs, issues opened outside the manifest) that the local
      tooling can't see.

      ## Triggers

      Three triggers in `.github/workflows/manifest-sync.yml`:

      1. **Scheduled (daily at 02:00 UTC)** — full reconcile pass. If drift
         exists, open a PR with manifest updates.
      2. **`pull_request.closed`** — if PR closed with `Closes #N` or
         `Fixes #N`, mark the manifest entry for issue N as `state: closed`
         with `closed_reason: "merged in PR #<num> on <date>"`.
      3. **`issues.closed`** — if a human closed an issue via the web UI,
         find its manifest entry and set `state: closed` with
         `closed_reason: "closed via GitHub UI on <date>"`.

      ## Script: scripts/manifest-sync.sh

      Two modes:
      - `--report` (read-only): prints drift to stdout
      - `--apply` (default in CI): edits manifest.yaml, opens PR via
        peter-evans/create-pull-request

      What it detects:
      - Live issues without a manifest entry → propose new manifest stub
        with title + labels + milestone (operator review required)
      - Manifest entries with `state: open` but live closed → propose
        `state: closed` + `closed_reason`
      - PRs that closed issues but the issue isn't in the manifest →
        append entry to `.github/issues/orphan-prs.md` log
      - Stale issues (no activity > 90 days, label: stale flag) → comment
        on the issue suggesting close-or-update

      ## Safety
      - Never auto-closes a live issue (read-only on GitHub side; only
        edits the local YAML and opens a PR)
      - Never auto-reopens
      - PR title prefixed `[manifest-sync]` so it's easy to filter / batch-review
      - Workflow uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` for issue/PR reads; needs `contents:write`
        + `pull-requests:write` for the auto-PR

      ## Dependencies
      - scripts/generate-issues.sh `--reconcile` mode (already implemented;
        sync-1 builds on this with the write-back logic)
      - peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6 action
    state: closed
    closed_reason: 'Closed manually on 2026-05-25. Implemented via PR #252 — .github/workflows/manifest-sync.yml and scripts/manifest-sync.sh both shipped.'

  - id: mutation-universalmutator-spike
    title: "Evaluate universalmutator for auto-generated bash mutation operators"
    milestone: "Phase 5 — Test Migration & Verification"
    labels: [phase-5, test-migration]
    state: open
    body: |
      Live issue: https://github.com/ezigus/zBuild/issues/325
      Spike to evaluate universalmutator (CMU, language-agnostic regex-driven
      mutation tool) as a complement to the hand-authored tests/mutation/*.md
      specs. Current harness (#298) is high-signal but low-coverage — only
      catches mutations someone thought to write.

      Define a small bash operator ruleset (==/!=, &&/||, drop set -e, swap
      -eq/-ne, flip exit codes, quoting strip), run against one keeper
      (e.g. core/router/route.sh), pipe each mutant through the test suite
      as oracle, and compare killed-mutant rate vs hand-written specs.

      Decide: keep both (hand-written for high-signal, auto-generated for
      breadth), fold one into the other, or drop.

      Out of scope: replacing hand-written specs wholesale; making
      universalmutator a hard CI dependency.

      Phase 5 because it's test-infrastructure tooling, not engine work;
      lands after Phase 0.5 stabilizes.

## Conflicts

### Conflicts (ADR-001 … ADR-008)

- **C1. ADR-001 §Hook signature vs ADR-001 §Error semantics and ADR-054 §4.** §Hook signature says plugins "MUST … return rc=2 if `state_file` is empty, so config errors surface distinctly". §Error semantics and ADR-054 §4 say plugin rc is binary (0/1). **The code follows binary**: `dispatch_rc_narrow` maps 2→1 (core/pipeline/dispatch-rc.sh:54; tests/unit/dispatch-rc-test.sh:67), so the "distinct" rc=2 can never be seen. About 40 plugin.sh files still `return 2` (e.g. plugins/agent/pr-delivery/plugin.sh:38).
- **C2. ADR-001 §Cross-plugin dependencies vs ADR-001 §requires.core (line 310) and ADR-051:172.** The first says `requires.plugins` "is enforced at discovery time"; the latter two say it "remains unlanded under #1321". **The code follows "unlanded"**: no resolver exists.
- **C3. ADR-003 §Migration rule vs code.** The ADR says `weight: 0` drains a candidate. core/router/route.sh:4,681 always takes `candidates[0]` and never reads `weight`. The router contract `route(tier, complexity, budget_state) → {…, fallback_chain}` also does not exist (route.sh:135).
- **C4. ADR-004 §Stage-level enforcement (and ADR-013's tier table) vs code.** Both list `pr` as T0, "MUST never emit LLM-bound text". `pr` is now delivered by plugins/agent/pr-delivery (`kind: agent`, `tier_default: T2`, manifest.yaml:3,31; #756). It makes no route call today, but its declared tier says otherwise.
- **C5. ADR-005 §Consequences vs ADR-056 / ADR-001 (amended).** ADR-005 relies on each coordinator's `init` hook to self-test. ADR-056 deleted `init`. The ADR-005 Implementation Notes still claim "flock … self-test in `init`: Implemented".
- **C6. ADR-001 §Lifecycle and ADR-006 §Resume sequence vs code.** Both tell plugins to check `ZBUILD_RESUMING=1`. Nothing sets it. The runner exports `ZBUILD_RESUME` (resume *intent*, default 1, tests/unit/resume-default-test.sh:55-57), a different variable with different meaning, so a plugin following the ADR never sees a resume.
- **C7. ADR-006 §Persisted vs code.** The ADR's headline fix (`current_iteration` survives resume) has no production writer; `write_plugin_state`/`read_plugin_state` and the `state.persisted` validation do not exist; step 3.5 (mid-cycle resume) is unimplemented. Cycle iteration state actually lives in `cycle_iterations` and cycle history JSONL, which ADR-006 lists only as an amendment.
- **C8. ADR-004 §The chokepoint vs code.** The ADR's signature is `<text_var> <manifest> <allowlist> <cycle_id>` and its `redaction.applied` payload is `{prompt_size, redactions_count, scope_hash, cycle_id}`. The code (scope-redaction.sh:40, :272-279) takes files `<input> <output> <manifest> [allowlist] [cycle]` and emits `size_before/size_after/redactions/scope_hash/cycle`. The ADR's "one-shot" override token is never consumed.
- **C9. ADR-002 §Pruning protocol vs legacy/migrated/.** The ADR requires a one-line tombstone. All 12 files are 21-65-line documents in three different shapes. ADR-002's Implementation Notes call security-lens pruned; its tombstone says "NOT pruned".
- **C10. ADR-007 vs code/CI.** It says nightly E2E (e2e actually runs per PR, with no nightly job), `ZBUILD_UPDATE_GOLDEN` (the variable is `UPDATE_GOLDEN`), and a re-source guard in every test (0 files have one). ADR-008 says "CI runs Node LTS 22" (no workflow sets a Node version).

### Conflicts (ADR-009..014)

- **C1 — ADR-009 §Backward-compat case 2 vs ADR-042 §2 and the code.**
  - ADR-009 says: if a stage declares roles but no plugin provides them, the runner tries the direct id match.
  - ADR-042 §2 says: declared but unresolved roles **fail closed** (rc=1).
  - core/pipeline/dispatch.sh:68-73 (`resolve_stage_plugin`, cycle and parallel paths) follows ADR-042, pinned by tests/unit/stage-resolution-parity-test.sh:115.
  - The leaf path still follows ADR-009: strategy rc=4 → `_find_plugin_for_stage` at core/pipeline/runner.sh:3875-3890. The resolvability preflight (template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh:295) may refuse first.
  - So two dispatch paths apply opposite rules, and ADR-009 was never marked amended.
- **C2 — ADR-011 §Graceful degradation rule 2 vs ADR-014 §Decision and the code.**
  - ADR-011 says: `fallback_to_default_on_error: false` → hard-fail with a clear error; `true` → fall back and emit `backend.degraded`.
  - ADR-014 says: backend load failures are non-fatal (warn and use stubs).
  - The code follows ADR-014, and goes further:
    - Memory gates the fallback on env `ZBUILD_MEMORY_FALLBACK`, not on the declared key (core/memory/contract.sh:63-76).
    - Orch and cache always fall back silently with no `backend.degraded` event (core/orch/contract.sh:175-181; core/cache/contract.sh `_zbuild_cache_load_backend`).
- **C3 — ADR-010 §3 (`gh-pr-comment` = one comment per run, edited in place) vs code.**
  - core/output/destinations.sh:58 posts a fresh `gh issue comment` on every `emit_output` call.
  - Only scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh follows the rule.
  - The check-run env var also differs: the ADR names `ZBUILD_EMIT_CHECK_RUN=true`, the code reads `ZBUILD_OUTPUT_GH_CHECK_RUN=1` (destinations.sh:66).
- **C4 — ADR-011 §Orchestrator (Phase 0.5 default = `orch-sequential`) vs code.**
  - core/config/config.sh:11 defaults to `bash-parallel`, pinned by tests/unit/core-config-load-test.sh:48.
  - The code follows `bash-parallel`.
- **C5 — ADR-011 §Retention ("the memory store is never reclaimed") vs code (suspected; verify).**
  - plugins/tool/memory-sqlite/plugin.sh:43-44 puts `memory.db` under `${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}` when it is set, and the runner exports ZBUILD_STATE_DIR = the run's state dir (core/pipeline/runner.sh:2141).
  - If that dir is per-run, `cleanup --state-dirs` (scripts/lib/cleanup.sh `_cleanup_scan_state_dirs`) would delete the memory store.
  - The enforcing test, cleanup-new-reclaimers-test.sh:197, greps cleanup.sh for the name and cannot see this.
- **C6 — ADR-009 §4 (`sequential` halts only if `per_platform_halt_on_fail: true`) vs code.**
  - core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh always halts, and the flag is not implemented.
- **C7 — ADR-009 §Auto-detection ("warn + skip the folder") vs code.**
  - core/detect/platforms.sh:424-430 substitutes `generic`; tests/unit/core-detect-platforms-a-test.sh:59 pins `generic`.
- **C8 — ADR-012 internal conflict.**
  - The Mutation convention says `--tier mutation` "validates doc structure (not behavior)", but the #1184 amendment and scripts/run-mutation.sh execute mutants.
  - The Coverage policy says "kcov over unit + integration", but scripts/check-coverage.sh traces `--tier unit` only, and the ADR's own 29% floor note contradicts check-coverage.sh's default of 70.
- **C9 — ADR-010 §1 `zbuild teardown` vs ADR-054 §7 / ADR-001 lifecycle (naming).**
  - ADR-010's CI `teardown` command (snapshot and upload) is unimplemented.
  - "teardown" now names ADR-054 §7's stage, which releases plugin `cleanup` hooks and is run by `zbuild clean`.
  - The two would collide if ADR-010 Phase 1 lands as written.

### Conflicts (ADR-013/015)

1. **ADR-013 §Stage sequence / §Template integration vs ADR-047 §5 (and code).** ADR-013 says unknown ids are rejected "at template-load time" and that order must follow the canonical sequence. ADR-047 demotes the list, and the code follows ADR-047:
   - `_ZBUILD_CANONICAL_STAGES` is deleted (core/pipeline/template.sh:23-29).
   - `load_template` accepts unknown ids (tests/unit/core-pipeline-template-test.sh:207).
   - Membership is enforced by the runner resolvability preflight, and order by the input DAG.
   - ADR-013's body still says reordering needs "a new ADR-013 revision".
2. **ADR-013 lifecycle_hooks column (`init, run, finalize`) vs ADR-001/ADR-056 (run + cleanup only).** The code follows ADR-056: the init hooks must not exist (tests/integration/deployed-template-e2e-test.sh:177).
3. **ADR-013 fail-closed rule vs code.** ADR-013 specifies a synthetic `stage.fail` with `reason: "missing_artifact"`. The code emits `plugin.artifact.missing`/`plugin.artifact.empty`, then `plugin.<hook>.error reason=artifact-check-failed` and `plugin.contract.violated` (core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh:103,505-512). No `missing_artifact` string exists in the code.
4. **ADR-013 #361 rule 3 ("canonical artifact MUST be first in `outputs[]`", `_check_artifact_contract`) vs ADR-047 §4 / code.** The checker is retired (artifact-enforcement-survives-retirement-test.sh:136), `primary: true` decides instead, and pr-open's first output is `pr_open_errors` (plugins/tool/pr-open/manifest.yaml:74).
5. **ADR-013 "downstream MUST NOT wire inputs from secondary artifacts" vs code.** merge reads `pr-result.json` (plugins/tool/merge/plugin.sh:97), and pr-delivery reads pr-open's `pr-result.json` (#2250). These are cross-plugin reads of the "secondary" file, though via delegation rather than a manifest `inputs:` edge.
6. **ADR-013 §Stage skip conditions vs code.** `stage.skip`, `disabled_stages` and `ZBUILD_MONITOR_ENABLED` are not implemented. `stage.skip` is only registered (config/event-schema.json:15). A resumed complete stage emits nothing named `stage.skip`.
7. **ADR-013 Decision table (`deploy`/`validate`/`pr` = `kind: tool`) vs the #757 amendment and code.** All three resolve to `kind: agent` plugins (plugins/agent/{deploy,validate,pr-delivery}). The ADR keeps the table "unchanged", so the doc contradicts itself.
8. **ADR-013 #1208 amendment (`verdict=did_not_finish`) vs ADR-054 / code.** `did_not_finish` was removed (core/pipeline/verdict.sh:111). Build writes `disposition: timed_out` (tests/unit/convergence-timeouts-never-fatal-1208-test.sh:339).
9. **ADR-013 #1208 amendment ("returns rc=2" path) vs ADR-054 §4 (binary plugin rc).** Historical only; the code follows ADR-054.
10. **ADR-015 §2 vs ADR-015 §F (internal) and code.** §2 says "nothing else writes to `state/artifacts/stage-io/`". §F (and core/router/route.sh:1136,2118) has the router write `<stage>-sync-error.*` / `-iter<N>-error.*` there directly, bypassing `capture_stage_io`, and plugins/agent/plan/plugin.sh:734 reads them.
11. **ADR-015 §v6 vs §5 (internal).** §v6 says per-iteration stage-io artifacts go to `state/artifacts/<stage>/`. §5 and the code use `state/artifacts/stage-io/<stage>-<seq>.json`.
12. **ADR-015 §v4 fd validation vs code.** The ADR says a not-open fd "aborts the `source`". The code (#586) warns and falls back to fd 2 (core/output/stage-io.sh:73-86), and a test pins the fallback (core-output-stage-io-fd-fallback-test.sh:46-47). The code follows #586.
13. **ADR-015 §H vs code.** The mandatory command capture is violated by pr-open, merge, deploy-release and github-labels, which run `gh`/`git` uncaptured.
14. **ADR-015 §6 vs code.** The `redact: false` opt-out "recorded in the artifact metadata" is not written into the record.
15. **ADR-015 Implementation Notes vs its own status.** The notes still say "Proposed … No code has been written". §v3's "turn the feature on in `config/templates/standard.yaml`" refers to a template retired by #979.

## Conflicts

### Conflicts (ADR-001 … ADR-008)

- **C1. ADR-001 §Hook signature vs ADR-001 §Error semantics and ADR-054 §4.** §Hook signature says plugins "MUST … return rc=2 if `state_file` is empty, so config errors surface distinctly". §Error semantics and ADR-054 §4 say plugin rc is binary (0/1). **The code follows binary**: `dispatch_rc_narrow` maps 2→1 (core/pipeline/dispatch-rc.sh:54; tests/unit/dispatch-rc-test.sh:67), so the "distinct" rc=2 can never be seen. About 40 plugin.sh files still `return 2` (e.g. plugins/agent/pr-delivery/plugin.sh:38).
- **C2. ADR-001 §Cross-plugin dependencies vs ADR-001 §requires.core (line 310) and ADR-051:172.** The first says `requires.plugins` "is enforced at discovery time"; the latter two say it "remains unlanded under #1321". **The code follows "unlanded"**: no resolver exists.
- **C3. ADR-003 §Migration rule vs code.** The ADR says `weight: 0` drains a candidate. core/router/route.sh:4,681 always takes `candidates[0]` and never reads `weight`. The router contract `route(tier, complexity, budget_state) → {…, fallback_chain}` also does not exist (route.sh:135).
- **C4. ADR-004 §Stage-level enforcement (and ADR-013's tier table) vs code.** Both list `pr` as T0, "MUST never emit LLM-bound text". `pr` is now delivered by plugins/agent/pr-delivery (`kind: agent`, `tier_default: T2`, manifest.yaml:3,31; #756). It makes no route call today, but its declared tier says otherwise.
- **C5. ADR-005 §Consequences vs ADR-056 / ADR-001 (amended).** ADR-005 relies on each coordinator's `init` hook to self-test. ADR-056 deleted `init`. The ADR-005 Implementation Notes still claim "flock … self-test in `init`: Implemented".
- **C6. ADR-001 §Lifecycle and ADR-006 §Resume sequence vs code.** Both tell plugins to check `ZBUILD_RESUMING=1`. Nothing sets it. The runner exports `ZBUILD_RESUME` (resume *intent*, default 1, tests/unit/resume-default-test.sh:55-57), a different variable with different meaning, so a plugin following the ADR never sees a resume.
- **C7. ADR-006 §Persisted vs code.** The ADR's headline fix (`current_iteration` survives resume) has no production writer; `write_plugin_state`/`read_plugin_state` and the `state.persisted` validation do not exist; step 3.5 (mid-cycle resume) is unimplemented. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh
# Synchronous mock orchestrator backend — test-only (issue #219).
#
# Work unit definition
# --------------------
# A "work unit" is a bash function body encoded as a plain string that is safe
# to pass through $(...) and environment variables without escaping.  Callers
# build one with the orch_work_unit helper below:
#
#   unit="$(orch_work_unit 'echo hello')"
#   pool_id="test-pool-$$"
#   orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$unit"
#   orch_collect  "$pool_id"
#
# Internally the mock stores each dispatched unit as a file under
# ${ORCH_MOCK_DIR}/<pool_id>/pending/<seq>.unit
# and writes results to
# ${ORCH_MOCK_DIR}/<pool_id>/results/<seq>.{stdout,rc}
# orch_collect reads them in order and prints the first non-zero rc + all stdout.
# orch_shutdown removes the pool directory.
#
# The mock NEVER spawns background subshells; every operation is synchronous.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_MOCK_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_MOCK_LOADED=1

# Root directory for all mock state.  Tests may set ORCH_MOCK_DIR before
# sourcing; otherwise it defaults to a subdirectory under TEST_TEMP_DIR (or /tmp).
ORCH_MOCK_DIR="${ORCH_MOCK_DIR:-${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-/tmp}/orch-mock}"

# ─── orch_work_unit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Build a work-unit string from a bash body fragment.
# Usage: unit="$(orch_work_unit 'echo "hello world"; exit 0')"
# The body must be expressible as a single-line string (no literal newlines
# in the argument).  For multi-statement bodies use semicolons.
orch_work_unit() {
    local body="$1"
    # Store as-is.  The body is what bash -c will receive.
    printf '%s' "$body"
}

# ─── _orch_mock_pool_dir ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
_orch_mock_pool_dir() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    # Sanitize pool_id: replace characters unsafe for directory names.
    local safe_id
    safe_id="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | tr -cs '[:alnum:]_-' '_')"
    echo "${ORCH_MOCK_DIR}/${safe_id}"
}

# ─── orch_spawn ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_spawn <pool_id> <count> <role_arg>
# Mock: creates the pool directory; count and role_arg are accepted but ignored
# because the mock runs work units as they are dispatched, not via pre-spawned
# workers.
orch_spawn() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    # $2 = count, $3 = role_arg — accepted, ignored in mock
    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"
    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/pending"
    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results"
    # Sequence counter for ordering
    printf '0' > "${pool_dir}/seq"
}

# ─── orch_dispatch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_dispatch <pool_id> <task_body>
# Mock: executes the task_body synchronously in a subshell; persists
#       stdout + exit code to results/<seq>.{stdout,rc}.
# Returns 0 (task accepted for execution); task failures surface via orch_collect.
# This matches the async contract: callers must not assume dispatch failure == task failure.
orch_dispatch() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    local task_body="$2"
    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"

    if [[ ! -d "${pool_dir}/pending" ]]; then
        # Auto-init pool if orch_spawn was not called explicitly.
        orch_spawn "$pool_id" 1 ""
    fi

    # Read and increment sequence counter.
    local seq
    seq="$(cat "${pool_dir}/seq" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    local next_seq=$(( seq + 1 ))
    printf '%s' "$next_seq" > "${pool_dir}/seq"

    local result_dir="${pool_dir}/results"
    local stdout_file="${result_dir}/${seq}.stdout"
    local rc_file="${result_dir}/${seq}.rc"

    # Execute synchronously; capture stdout; store rc.
    local task_rc=0
    bash -c "$task_body" > "$stdout_file" 2>&1 || task_rc=$?
    printf '%s' "$task_rc" > "$rc_file"

    # Always return 0: dispatch means "task accepted", not "task succeeded".
    # Task failures are surfaced by orch_collect, preserving set -e safety.
    return 0
}

# ─── orch_collect ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_collect <pool_id> [--timeout S]
# Mock: iterates all result files in dispatch order; prints stdout of every
#       work unit.  Returns per the orch contract (#269, #1850):
#         0 — all work units exited 0 (success)
#         1 — otherwise; _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME names it `failed` (all exited
#             non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed) — once rc 2
#       --timeout is accepted but ignored (mock is synchronous).
orch_collect() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    # Accept --timeout flag without error; value is discarded.
    # shift remaining args — nothing to parse beyond pool_id for the mock.

    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    if [[ ! -d "${pool_dir}/results" ]]; then
        # Pool was never initialized — nothing to collect.
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    fi

    local total
    total="$(cat "${pool_dir}/seq" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
    local i
    for (( i = 0; i < total; i++ )); do
        local stdout_file="${pool_dir}/results/${i}.stdout"
        local rc_file="${pool_dir}/results/${i}.rc"

        if [[ -f "$stdout_file" ]]; then
            cat "$stdout_file"
        fi

        if [[ -f "$rc_file" ]]; then
            local task_rc
            task_rc="$(cat "$rc_file")"
            if [[ "$task_rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
                pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
            else
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
            fi
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi
}

# ─── orch_shutdown ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_shutdown <pool_id>
# Mock: removes the pool directory completely.
orch_shutdown() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"
    if [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
    fi
}

# ─── orch_capabilities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_capabilities → JSON array of declared capabilities.
# Mock: returns the capabilities declared in the manifest.
orch_capabilities() {
    printf '["sequential","fanout"]\n'
}

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Convenience function checked by the contract layer (core/orch/contract.sh).
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities)"
    # Simple grep-based check — no jq required for the mock.
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── Lifecycle hooks (used by plugin_hook_call) ───────────────────────────────
orch_mock_run() {
    # No-op for the mock; real backends would do daemon startup here.
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh
# Synchronous mock orchestrator backend — test-only (issue #219).
#
# Work unit definition
# --------------------
# A "work unit" is a bash function body encoded as a plain string that is safe
# to pass through $(...) and environment variables without escaping.  Callers
# build one with the orch_work_unit helper below:
#
#   unit="$(orch_work_unit 'echo hello')"
#   pool_id="test-pool-$$"
#   orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$unit"
#   orch_collect  "$pool_id"
#
# Internally the mock stores each dispatched unit as a file under
# ${ORCH_MOCK_DIR}/<pool_id>/pending/<seq>.unit
# and writes results to
# ${ORCH_MOCK_DIR}/<pool_id>/results/<seq>.{stdout,rc}
# orch_collect reads them in order and prints the first non-zero rc + all stdout.
# orch_shutdown removes the pool directory.
#
# The mock NEVER spawns background subshells; every operation is synchronous.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_MOCK_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_MOCK_LOADED=1

# Root directory for all mock state.  Tests may set ORCH_MOCK_DIR before
# sourcing; otherwise it defaults to a subdirectory under TEST_TEMP_DIR (or /tmp).
ORCH_MOCK_DIR="${ORCH_MOCK_DIR:-${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-/tmp}/orch-mock}"

# ─── orch_work_unit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Build a work-unit string from a bash body fragment.
# Usage: unit="$(orch_work_unit 'echo "hello world"; exit 0')"
# The body must be expressible as a single-line string (no literal newlines
# in the argument).  For multi-statement bodies use semicolons.
orch_work_unit() {
    local body="$1"
    # Store as-is.  The body is what bash -c will receive.
    printf '%s' "$body"
}

# ─── _orch_mock_pool_dir ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
_orch_mock_pool_dir() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    # Sanitize pool_id: replace characters unsafe for directory names.
    local safe_id
    safe_id="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | tr -cs '[:alnum:]_-' '_')"
    echo "${ORCH_MOCK_DIR}/${safe_id}"
}

# ─── orch_spawn ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_spawn <pool_id> <count> <role_arg>
# Mock: creates the pool directory; count and role_arg are accepted but ignored
# because the mock runs work units as they are dispatched, not via pre-spawned
# workers.
orch_spawn() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    # $2 = count, $3 = role_arg — accepted, ignored in mock
    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"
    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/pending"
    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results"
    # Sequence counter for ordering
    printf '0' > "${pool_dir}/seq"
}

# ─── orch_dispatch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_dispatch <pool_id> <task_body>
# Mock: executes the task_body synchronously in a subshell; persists
#       stdout + exit code to results/<seq>.{stdout,rc}.
# Returns 0 (task accepted for execution); task failures surface via orch_collect.
# This matches the async contract: callers must not assume dispatch failure == task failure.
orch_dispatch() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    local task_body="$2"
    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"

    if [[ ! -d "${pool_dir}/pending" ]]; then
        # Auto-init pool if orch_spawn was not called explicitly.
        orch_spawn "$pool_id" 1 ""
    fi

    # Read and increment sequence counter.
    local seq
    seq="$(cat "${pool_dir}/seq" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    local next_seq=$(( seq + 1 ))
    printf '%s' "$next_seq" > "${pool_dir}/seq"

    local result_dir="${pool_dir}/results"
    local stdout_file="${result_dir}/${seq}.stdout"
    local rc_file="${result_dir}/${seq}.rc"

    # Execute synchronously; capture stdout; store rc.
    local task_rc=0
    bash -c "$task_body" > "$stdout_file" 2>&1 || task_rc=$?
    printf '%s' "$task_rc" > "$rc_file"

    # Always return 0: dispatch means "task accepted", not "task succeeded".
    # Task failures are surfaced by orch_collect, preserving set -e safety.
    return 0
}

# ─── orch_collect ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_collect <pool_id> [--timeout S]
# Mock: iterates all result files in dispatch order; prints stdout of every
#       work unit.  Returns per the orch contract (#269, #1850):
#         0 — all work units exited 0 (success)
#         1 — otherwise; _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME names it `failed` (all exited
#             non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed) — once rc 2
#       --timeout is accepted but ignored (mock is synchronous).
orch_collect() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    # Accept --timeout flag without error; value is discarded.
    # shift remaining args — nothing to parse beyond pool_id for the mock.

    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    if [[ ! -d "${pool_dir}/results" ]]; then
        # Pool was never initialized — nothing to collect.
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    fi

    local total
    total="$(cat "${pool_dir}/seq" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
    local i
    for (( i = 0; i < total; i++ )); do
        local stdout_file="${pool_dir}/results/${i}.stdout"
        local rc_file="${pool_dir}/results/${i}.rc"

        if [[ -f "$stdout_file" ]]; then
            cat "$stdout_file"
        fi

        if [[ -f "$rc_file" ]]; then
            local task_rc
            task_rc="$(cat "$rc_file")"
            if [[ "$task_rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
                pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
            else
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
            fi
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi
}

# ─── orch_shutdown ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_shutdown <pool_id>
# Mock: removes the pool directory completely.
orch_shutdown() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"
    if [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
    fi
}

# ─── orch_capabilities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_capabilities → JSON array of declared capabilities.
# Mock: returns the capabilities declared in the manifest.
orch_capabilities() {
    printf '["sequential","fanout"]\n'
}

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Convenience function checked by the contract layer (core/orch/contract.sh).
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities)"
    # Simple grep-based check — no jq required for the mock.
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── Lifecycle hooks (used by plugin_hook_call) ───────────────────────────────
orch_mock_run() {
    # No-op for the mock; real backends would do daemon startup here.
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: engine defaults land under the data root, never ${TMPDIR} (#2004).
#
# ADR-059 §1 makes the path the keying — a reclaimer deletes a `runs/<id>/` or
# an `issues/<N>/` and the scope follows from where it sits. A default that
# writes into ${TMPDIR} is outside every reclaimable path BY CONSTRUCTION: there
# is nothing for a reclaimer to name. ADR-023 and ADR-059 §1 also reject
# ${TMPDIR} for durable state on measured evidence — on macOS its entries can
# vanish mid-run (#1571, #1609/#1611).
#
# Measured before this change: 3063 zbuild-* directories (180 MB) had
# accumulated on one developer machine, ~2300 of them zbuild-ephemeral-events.*.
# `cleanup.sh`'s ZBUILD_TMPDIR_PATTERNS scanner exists to sweep them, which
# makes it a workaround for these defaults rather than a feature.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "ADR-059: engine defaults are reclaimable, not \${TMPDIR}-rooted (#2004)"
setup_test_env "adr059-no-tmpdir"

FAKE_TMP="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fake-tmp"; mkdir -p "$FAKE_TMP"
DATA_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/data-root"; mkdir -p "$DATA_ROOT"

# ─── SPEC-1: the unpinned event-bus dir is under the data root ──────────────
# Nothing pinned is the ad-hoc/test path; it produced ~2300 leaked dirs.
_s1="$(env -u ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR -u ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL -u ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB \
        TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
        bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; printf "%s" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"')"
case "$_s1" in
    "$DATA_ROOT"/*) assert_pass "[SPEC-1] unpinned event dir is under the data root" ;;
    "$FAKE_TMP"/*)  assert_fail "[SPEC-1] unpinned event dir is under the data root" \
                        "landed in \$TMPDIR — unreclaimable by construction: $_s1" ;;
    *)              assert_fail "[SPEC-1] unpinned event dir is under the data root" "got: $_s1" ;;
esac

# ─── SPEC-2: an explicit pin still wins ────────────────────────────────────
# The fix must not override an operator's or the runner's explicit choice.
_s2="$(env -u ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL -u ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB \
        TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pinned" \
        bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; printf "%s" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"')"
assert_eq "[SPEC-2] an explicit ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR pin still wins" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pinned" "$_s2"

# ─── SPEC-3: pool dirs sit under the run's state dir ───────────────────────
# ADR-059 §1 places them at runs/<run_id>/pool/. ZBUILD_STATE_DIR already
# resolves to runs/<run_id>/ under the issue (or goal) area.
STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/issues/42/runs/r1"; mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
_s3="$(env -u ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" ZBUILD_RUN_ID="r1" \
        bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/plugin.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; _orch_par_pool_dir p1')"
case "$_s3" in
    "$STATE_DIR"/pool/*) assert_pass "[SPEC-3] bash-parallel pool dir is under runs/<run_id>/pool" ;;
    "$FAKE_TMP"/*)       assert_fail "[SPEC-3] bash-parallel pool dir is under runs/<run_id>/pool" \
                             "landed in \$TMPDIR: $_s3" ;;
    *)                   assert_fail "[SPEC-3] bash-parallel pool dir is under runs/<run_id>/pool" "got: $_s3" ;;
esac

# ─── SPEC-4: the mock backend uses ORCH_MOCK_DIR (sequential backend retired) ──
# orch-mock is the test-time replacement for the retired sequential backend.
# Its pool dir is ORCH_MOCK_DIR/<pool_id>; in test contexts ORCH_MOCK_DIR defaults
# to $TEST_TEMP_DIR/orch-mock (not $TMPDIR).
_s4_expected="${TEST_TEMP_DIR}/orch-mock/p1"
_s4="$(env -u ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" ZBUILD_RUN_ID="r1" \
        bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; _orch_mock_pool_dir p1')"
if [[ "$_s4" == "$_s4_expected" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] mock pool dir is ORCH_MOCK_DIR/p1 (not under \$TMPDIR)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] mock pool dir is ORCH_MOCK_DIR/p1 (not under \$TMPDIR)" \
        "expected: $_s4_expected, got: $_s4"
fi

# ─── SPEC-5: an explicit ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT still wins ───────────────────────
_s5="$(TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pinned-pool" \
        bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/plugin.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; _orch_par_pool_dir p1')"
assert_eq "[SPEC-5] an explicit ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT pin still wins" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pinned-pool/zbuild-pool-p1" "$_s5"

# ─── SPEC-6 (#2004 audit): the ruflo-hive backend agrees with the other two ─
# It was missed when the bash-parallel and sequential backends were fixed, and
# it is worse than they were: no per-run namespace at all, and `zbuild-hive-*`
# is absent from ZBUILD_TMPDIR_PATTERNS, so nothing swept it either.
_s6="$(env -u ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" ZBUILD_RUN_ID="r1" \
        bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; _orch_hive_pool_dir p1')"
case "$_s6" in
    "$STATE_DIR"/pool/*) assert_pass "[SPEC-6] ruflo-hive pool dir is under runs/<run_id>/pool" ;;
    "$FAKE_TMP"/*)       assert_fail "[SPEC-6] ruflo-hive pool dir is under runs/<run_id>/pool" \
                             "landed in \$TMPDIR: $_s6" ;;
    *)                   assert_fail "[SPEC-6] ruflo-hive pool dir is under runs/<run_id>/pool" "got: $_s6" ;;
esac

# ─── SPEC-7: an explicit ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT still wins for hive too ──────────
_s7="$(TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pinned-hive" \
        bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; _orch_hive_pool_dir p1')"
assert_eq "[SPEC-7] hive honours an explicit ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/pinned-hive/zbuild-hive-p1" "$_s7"

# ─── SPEC-8: with NO state dir at all, the fallback is still reclaimable ────
# The ad-hoc/test caller. This arm used to root in ${TMPDIR}, which quietly
# reintroduced the leak the rest of this file exists to prevent — the event bus
# and the pool backends had answered the same question two different ways.
for _b in orch-bash-parallel orch-ruflo-hive; do
    _fn="_orch_par_pool_dir"
    [[ "$_b" == "orch-ruflo-hive" ]] && _fn="_orch_hive_pool_dir"
    _s8="$(env -u ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT -u ZBUILD_STATE_DIR -u ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT \
            TMPDIR="$FAKE_TMP" ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" ZBUILD_RUN_ID="r1" \
            bash -c 'source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/plugins/tool/'"$_b"'/plugin.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; '"$_fn"' p1')"
    case "$_s8" in
        "$DATA_ROOT"/*) assert_pass "[SPEC-8] $_b falls back to the data root, not \$TMPDIR" ;;
        "$FAKE_TMP"/*)  assert_fail "[SPEC-8] $_b falls back to the data root, not \$TMPDIR" \
                            "landed in \$TMPDIR: $_s8" ;;
        *)              assert_fail "[SPEC-8] $_b falls back to the data root, not \$TMPDIR" "got: $_s8" ;;
    esac
done

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"

print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
_prep timeout
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
_tbin=""
if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
fi
if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
else
    # #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own teardown
    # budget, not guessed.
    #
    # The engine bounds each always-run stage by its template `stage_timeout_s`,
    # falling back to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30s) only when the template
    # sets none (#2287) — so the pin below is a fallback, and this case relies on
    # its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound. Three stages
    # release on this path, so an unpinned run is entitled to spend far longer
    # tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here. When it did, this
    # test SIGKILLed the runner mid-teardown and then asserted on the markers
    # teardown had not yet written: the marker came back EMPTY, with BOTH stages
    # missing rather than one. Under a loaded machine that is exactly what
    # happened, intermittently, for as long as this test has existed.
    #
    # Pin the budget so the worst case is knowable, then clear it with margin.
    # The backstop exists so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite —
    # it must never be the thing that stops teardown finishing.
    _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=3
    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
    set -m
    ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S="$_SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _spec5_killer=$!
    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
fi

# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
# case is only about what survives it.
_prep blocking-ignore-term
export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-ignore-term" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
set -e
unset BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM
_child_pid=""
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
done
_alive=1
# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results

_runner_dispatch_always_run() {
        [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" && -f "${_runner_state_file}" ]] || return 0
        [[ "${#_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN[@]}" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
        local plugins_root="${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}"
        local _ar_stage _ar_safe _ar_role _ar_to _ar_dir _ar_guard
        for _ar_stage in "${_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN[@]}"; do
            _ar_safe="${_ar_stage//-/_}"
            # Per-stage, not global: the trap can be reached more than once, and
            # there is now more than one always-run stage to keep track of.
            _ar_guard="_RUNNER_AR_DISPATCHED_${_ar_safe}"
            [[ "${!_ar_guard:-0}" == "1" ]] && continue
            printf -v "$_ar_guard" '%s' 1

            local _ar_roles_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_${_ar_safe}"
            _ar_role="${!_ar_roles_var:-}"
            [[ -n "$_ar_role" ]] || continue
            # roles: is a list; an always-run stage takes the first.
            _ar_role="${_ar_role%%,*}"

            _ar_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$_ar_role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [[ -z "$_ar_dir" || ! -d "$_ar_dir" ]]; then
                # LOUD, unlike the old `[[ -d ... ]] || return 0`. An always-run
                # stage that cannot be resolved has not run, and the operator
                # needs to know that rather than infer it from a missing effect.
                eb_emit_event "stage.always_run.unresolved" "stage=$_ar_stage" "role=$_ar_role" 2>/dev/null || true
                continue
            fi

            local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_${_ar_safe}"
            _ar_to="${!_ar_to_var:-}"
            [[ "$_ar_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ar_to" -gt 0 ]] || _ar_to="${ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S:-30}"
            [[ "$_ar_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ar_to" -gt 0 ]] || _ar_to=30

            # Load process-group kill helpers if not already loaded.
            if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi

            # Bounded, because this runs inside the EXIT trap: a hook that blocks
            # would turn a Ctrl-C into a hang — the exact class of bug this
            # mechanism exists to prevent. A timeout BINARY cannot be used here
            # (plugin_hook_call is a shell function; timeout can only exec a
            # command, so the wrapper would fail with "command not found" and
            # silently skip every dispatch). The bound is therefore a watchdog
            # that is CANCELLED on the normal path, so no stray `sleep` outlives
            # the run.
            #
            # `|| true` because an always-run stage's failure is recorded as an
            # event and must NEVER change the run's exit status.
            #
            # #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it.
            # Signalling the one PID reached only the outer shell: the subshell
            # running the stage hooks, and anything it spawned, lived on after
            # the run and wrote into its state minutes later. `set -m` (as the
            # router's model spawn does, #2056) makes each job a process-group
            # leader, so zbuild_pg_kill reaches the whole tree — TERM + 10 s
            # grace + KILL. The watchdog gets its own group too, so cancelling
            # it leaves no `sleep` behind.
            (
                export ZBUILD_TEARDOWN_SCOPE=release
                set -m
                plugin_hook_call "$_ar_dir" run "$_ar_stage" "$_runner_state_file" &
                _ar_pid=$!
                ( set +m; sleep "$_ar_to"; zbuild_pg_kill "$_ar_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true ) &
                _wd_pid=$!
                set +m
                wait "$_ar_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                # #2333: the leader exiting does not mean its group did. A member
                # that ignored TERM would lose its KILL when the watchdog is
                # cancelled below, so KILL the group now; a no-op when it is gone.
                kill -KILL -- -"$_ar_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                kill -TERM -- -"$_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                wait "$_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        done
        return 0
    }

    _runner_abort_trap() {
        # #1829: free live resources first, while the state file and the
        # process tree are still intact.
        _runner_dispatch_always_run
        # #1688: release the issue lock EXPLICITLY. Relying on process death is
        # not enough — a flock belongs to the open file description, which every
        # child inherits, so one lingering child would keep the issue locked
        # after this run is gone. Released after the always-run stages, which
        # still belong to this run.
        if declare -F zbuild_issue_lock_release >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            zbuild_issue_lock_release || true
        fi
